claims.text: The `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct, enforced entirely within Pulumi and never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes that the cloud provider enforces independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider-enforced deletion-protection attribute separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider-enforced deletion-protection attribute separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (i.e. the `protect` option is not set) and still refuse to delete due to the cloud provider's own deletion-protection attribute.
A resource can have Pulumi's `protect` option set and still be deletable at the cloud-provider level (i.e. protected in Pulumi but not protected by the cloud provider), or vice versa.

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/#deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself exists and explains how to distinguish Pulumi's `protect` option from a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attribute and how to resolve each.
Pulumi has no single flag to protect every resource in a stack.
Stack transforms can be used to set the `protect` option on every resource in a stack as it's registered.
The `protect` resource option guards a resource within Pulumi.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the provider or cloud API, separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the provider or cloud API, separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attribute are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' section explains how to tell Pulumi's `protect` option apart from a resource's own deletion-protection attribute and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Where `protect` refuses to delete a resource, `retainOnDelete` takes the opposite approach.
`retainOnDelete` lets Pulumi remove a resource from state without calling the provider's delete operation, leaving the underlying cloud resource in place.
`retainOnDelete` is the right choice when you want to stop managing a resource with Pulumi, or hand it off, without destroying its data.
A `pulumi destroy` failure is often not an engine problem: the resource itself is guarded against deletion by something that must be removed before Pulumi can delete it.
Three distinct layers can hold deletion protection on a resource, and the error message usually indicates which layer was hit.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
An error naming a URN and mentioning `protect` indicates the Pulumi `protect` resource option, documented at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/.
Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute.
The `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute.
The `gcp.container.Cluster` resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute.
When a provider-enforced deletion-protection flag blocks deletion, the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves, independent of Pulumi.
AWS RDS has a `deletionProtection` attribute that can cause a cloud-API-enforced deletion protection.
AWS EC2 has a `disableApiTermination` attribute that can cause a cloud-API-enforced deletion protection.
An Azure Resource Manager management lock can cause a cloud-API-enforced deletion protection.
When a cloud-API-enforced protection blocks deletion, the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently specifies.
Setting a deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program alone is not sufficient to allow `pulumi destroy` to succeed.

The remediation for provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection is the same: set the deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches both the live resource and Pulumi's state, then run `pulumi destroy`.
Running `pulumi up` propagates a deletion-protection change to both the live resource and Pulumi's state.
If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g., directly in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality.
After a `pulumi refresh` synchronizes state following an out-of-band protection change, `pulumi destroy` succeeds without needing an intervening `pulumi up`.
The `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource's deletion protection via `deletionProtection` is provider-enforced.
The `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
The `gcp.container.Cluster` resource's `deletionProtection` attribute is provider-enforced.
The `gcp.bigquery.Table` resource has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
The `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` resource has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is set to `true`.
The `aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` resources have a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the AWS API.
The `deletionProtection` attribute on `aws.rds.Instance`/`aws.rds.Cluster` defaults to `false`.
The `aws.s3.BucketV2` resource has a `forceDestroy` attribute.
The `forceDestroy` attribute on `aws.s3.BucketV2` defaults to `false`.
A non-empty `aws.s3.BucketV2` bucket otherwise fails to delete when `forceDestroy` is not set to `true`.
The `aws.ec2.Instance` resource has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced by the AWS API as EC2 termination protection.
The `aws.dynamodb.Table` resource has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute enforced by the AWS API.
The `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute on `aws.dynamodb.Table` defaults to `false`.
Azure resources under a management lock are protected via `azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and its scope-specific variants, e.g. `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel`.
Azure management locks are enforced by Azure Resource Manager.
A `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before an Azure resource under it can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.
The `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` resource has soft delete and purge protection features.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Purge protection on `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` prevents purging until its retention period elapses.
